headline: Elevation requires sustained effort against gravity—but height provides perspective and advantage
universal_truth: Going up is hard; that's why high ground is valuable; the effort creates the advantage
fun_facts: Climbing stairs burns about 0.17 calories per step—going up requires 5x more energy than walking on flat ground
Mount Everest's summit has only 33% of sea-level oxygen—height has costs as well as benefits
The world's longest escalator is 453 feet—we build tools to make elevation easier
discussion_questions: Where in your life are you trying to 'go up'?
What's the view from the heights you've achieved?
When is the climb worth the effort?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Climbing stairs leaves you winded. Climbing mountains leaves you exhausted. Going up fights gravity—it costs energy. But height provides advantage: better view, strategic position, achievement. The effort creates the value.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We use 'up' metaphorically: rising to challenges, climbing the ladder, reaching the top. Why is elevation so central to how we think about achievement?
cliff.prompt: Why do we associate up with better?

options.text: Height provides real advantages—better view, strategic position, harder for others to reach—and the effort required creates scarcity, making heights valuable
options.response: Yes. High ground is valuable precisely because it's hard to reach. The effort filters out those who won't pay the cost. Difficulty is part of the value.

options.text: It's just a metaphor—up has no real advantage
options.response: It's metaphorical, but rooted in real physics—height does provide advantages...

q1.title: Fighting Gravity
q1.script: Going up means working against Earth's gravity. Every foot of elevation requires lifting your weight that distance. It's never free. This is why elevation costs energy—it's physics, not weakness.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Fighting Gravity"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Height Advantages
q2.script: Height provides perspective—you see more from above. It provides safety—threats are below. It provides achievement—others can see you've climbed. These advantages justify the cost.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Sustainable Ascent
q3.script: You can't sprint up a mountain—sustainable climbing requires pacing. The same in life: rapid rises exhaust you. Steady climbing, with rest, reaches higher than burst-and-crash approaches.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Going up is hard—that's why high ground is valuable. The effort creates the advantage. Climb steadily, climb sustainably.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 230! Tomorrow, we'll explore making structures—engineering. Until then, assess where you're climbing and whether your pace is sustainable.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Climb Assessment - Where Are You Going Up?
growTrack.activity: Where in your life are you 'climbing'—working toward elevation? Is the pace sustainable? What's the view from where you are now? Sometimes pausing to appreciate progress gives energy for the next stage of the climb.
